nodes.description: Public address state variable that stores the privileged governance role of the CurveI contract.
Public mapping of addresses flagged as minters; declared but never mutated in this contract.
CurveI constructor that assigns msg.sender to governance and mints the initial 10000*10**18 supply to that address.
Caller-supplied address (msg.sender) used to seed the privileged governance role.
Internal _mint that creates the total supply and credits it to governance, a privileged and irreversible state-changing operation.
Constructor parameter 'name' used to initialize ERC20Detailed._name.
Constructor parameter 'symbol' used to initialize ERC20Detailed._symbol.
Constructor parameter 'decimals' used to initialize ERC20Detailed._decimals.

edges.reason: msg.sender is read inside the CurveI constructor to perform the initial configuration.
Untrusted caller address (msg.sender) is written into the privileged governance state variable without any authorization check, allowing anyone deploying the contract to seize the governance role.
The governance address is passed as the recipient argument to _mint, so the minted supply is credited to the governance holder.
The constructor invokes _mint to create the initial token supply during deployment.
The 'name' constructor argument flows into the CurveI/ERC20Detailed initialization.
The 'symbol' constructor argument flows into the CurveI/ERC20Detailed initialization.
The 'decimals' constructor argument flows into the CurveI/ERC20Detailed initialization.

normalization_plan.reason: The name parameter is only a constructor input used to set token metadata; it carries no independent state and can be folded into the constructor function node.
The symbol parameter is only a constructor input for token metadata and has no standalone semantic role.
The decimals parameter is only a constructor input for token metadata and can be represented within its constructor function node.
